title: A scripted orchestrator conforms to the contract; ai relay --json carries the machine-readable parts

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: v8 assumes the orchestrator is an LLM agent briefed with `ai relay-orchestrator`. ork's engine is a deterministic orchestrator: it spawns roles, records the ledger and stops on the stop rules in code. The retrospective (R3) found most of the run's friction in the LLM orchestrator layer: broken no-cd rules, empty hand-backs, an API error mid-gate (S33), fragile headless resume. The contract has no statement of what a program must do to conform, so ork restates the contract in its own docs, and the two drift. s379 (`check_command`) and s387 (pin) already expose parts as JSON.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/ai.py`: a Conformance section; the `ai relay --json` payload.
- `docs/agents.md`: the JSON shape.
- The contract golden fixture.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. A short Conformance section: the obligations any orchestrator has (role order, gate rule, stop rules, ledger steps, finish step only after PASS, run report lines), whether an agent or a program.
2. `ai relay --json` carries those parts as data: roles, the order, gate criteria, stop rules, finding kinds, the run report fields, `check_command` (s379) and the version (s387).
